packages.label: אֱמוּנָה וֶאֱלֹקֵי אָבִיךָ
packages.label_en: Faith and the God of Your Father
packages.reason: The single bechina-connected component in Torah #94 equates אֱמוּנָה (faith) with אֱלֹקֵי אָבִיךָ ('the God of your father'). The Rebbe derives this from the Talmudic principle 'מַעֲשֵׂה אֲבוֹתֵיהֶם בִּידֵיהֶם' (Chullin 13b) — the ancestral practice is in their hands, meaning: our faith IS the inherited tradition of believing in the God of our fathers. The proof text reads: 'וֶאֱלֹקֵי אָבִיךָ, הִיא בְחִינַת אֱמוּנָה'. The two nodes share exactly the same essential nature: trust in the God who revealed Himself to the patriarchs, the root-faith that precedes intellectual investigation. This is the good/holy domain — it is the positive foundation of the teaching. In Torah #94 the Rebbe presents אמונה as the seventh quality (השביעית), parallel to Shabbat, which is added to the six days of action (עשייה = ששת ימי החול). This framing places faith in the transcendent/holy domain.
